title: JSSC-CGL exam cancellation ends one protest, sparks another as 2,000 fear job loss
content: Successful JSSC-CGL candidates protested the Jharkhand government's decision to cancel recruitment exams.  They fear losing their government jobs after the cancellation announcement on Monday night.  Protesters demanded a CBI probe and an opportunity to defend themselves against allegations.  The government defended the cancellation to restore confidence in the recruitment system.  Fresh vacancies will provide opportunities for deserving candidates after reforms.

title: Rishabh Pant creates history, becomes first Indian to achieve this feat
content: India's star wicketkeeper batter Rishabh Pant created history on Tuesday during the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle. The India wicketkeeper-batter became the first Indian cricketer to hit 100 sixes in Test cricket. Pant reached the milestone with a big six off Lahiru Kumara. The shot also brought up his 20th Test fifty.

title: No chemistry teacher: Gen alpha students protest at Azamgarh school
content: Students protested their Azamgarh college, citing excessive fees and teacher shortages. They demanded a chemistry teacher, receiving assurances of one within forty-eight hours. Allegations of unreturned funds and management issues were also raised by supporters. The students seek fair treatment and better academic facilities from the institution. They warned of renewed protests if the chemistry teacher is not provided promptly.

title: With no 'China burden' like on Apple, Google to stop making Pixel devices in the country
content: Google is gearing up to transition its Pixel production away from China starting next year. This move is aimed at mitigating risks linked to geopolitical tensions, with new manufacturing hubs being established in Vietnam and India. The company is looking to enhance its shipment volume for Pixel devices, placing a strong focus on advancements in artificial intelligence, strategically positioning itself in a competitive market.

title: Why India is considering sugar imports as prices hit record levels
content: India is considering limited duty-free sugar imports and tighter stock limits. These measures aim to boost domestic supplies and control record high sugar prices. Wholesale sugar prices have climbed nearly twenty percent since early August. Festival season demand typically increases sweetener consumption sharply each year. The government is examining several policy options to manage market conditions.

title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40B in medical debt; how mechanics work
content: MacKenzie Scott's donations have enabled medical debt abolition across America. Her approach allows acquiring and erasing patient debt at steep discounts. This model has inspired other billionaires to contribute millions to similar initiatives. While philanthropic efforts provide immediate relief, policy reform remains stalled. Lasting change may require systemic reforms addressing the root causes of medical debt.

title: Video: VCK protest turns violent after TN cop slaps passing man, he retaliates
content: A Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi protest in Thanjavur escalated into violence.  A police officer slapped a man who attempted to pass through the blockade.  The man retaliated by slapping the officer back during the heated exchange.  Police intervened and forcibly arrested the man after he refused to cooperate.  Authorities stated minimal force was used to contain the situation and prevent escalation.

title: Apple buried about 2,700 Lisa computers in 1989 in a landfill; here's why
content: In 1989, Apple buried about 2,700 unsold Lisa computers at a landfill in Logan, Utah, ending the story of one of its biggest early failures. Launched in 1983 with a graphical interface and mouse, the Lisa was ahead of its time but struggled because of its nearly $10,000 price and hardware problems. A computer reseller later tried to upgrade and sell thousands of the machines, but the effort ultimately failed. Today, surviving Lisa computers are valuable pieces of Apple history.

title: Jeanne Socrates was injured at 75; two years later she sailed solo around world
content: At the inspiring age of 77, British sailor Jeanne Socrates completed a solo, non-stop circumnavigation of the globe. Starting her journey aboard the yacht Nereida from Victoria, Canada, in 2018, she faced tumultuous seas for 320 days. Socrates bravely overcame significant challenges, including repairs and injuries from a serious fall sustained earlier.

title: Google buys a dead airline's data for $10 million, but here's what it's not getting
content: Google has won a bankruptcy auction for Spirit Airlines' internal business data with a $10 million bid, beating AI firm Mercor, and says the trove will help train its AI models. The company clarified it is not buying customer or credit card information. Filings list 100 million emails, 500 million Teams chats and 30 million lines of code. A judge considers the Spirit Airlines data sale on August 19.

title: Hingoli ZP school headmaster accused of being drunk in classes suspended
content: A headmaster from a primary school has been suspended amid allegations of intoxication and negligence towards his teaching duties. Complaints poured in from students and parents regarding his lack of proper class management. His unsatisfactory answers to the show-cause notice led to this suspension order, sparked by a campaign initiated by Abhijeet Dipke in Hingoli. He is now subject to disciplinary actions governed by Maharashtra Zilla Parishad rules.

title: Knee-surgery beneficiaries dance at Punjab I-Day function sparks political slugfest
content: A video showcasing elderly men dancing at Punjab's Independence Day celebrations has sparked a heated political discussion. Opposition leaders claim these men were actually employees from the health department rather than beneficiaries of social schemes. In contrast, the Aam Aadmi Party defends the dance as a positive expression.

title: 'Batwara 1947' BO collection Day 5 [LIVE]: Sunny Deol starrer eyes to surpass Rs 30 cr
content: 'Batwara 1947', starring Sunny Deol, accumulated Rs 0.40 crore on its fifth day, with an impressive opening weekend collection of Rs 26.50 crore. The film's total earnings in India now reach Rs 28.90 crore. As it enters the competitive landscape of 'Awarapan 2' and 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day', it continues to showcase its appeal following its release on August 14, 2026.

title: ‘He quit his job’: Unnati’s emotional tribute to father after World C'ships debut win
content: Making a remarkable debut at the BWF World Championships, Unnati Hooda scored a swift victory in straight games. She expressed heartfelt thanks to her father, who sacrificed his career to coach her diligently. Inspired by Ayush Shetty's surprising triumph over a top competitor, Unnati is determined to focus on her performance and give her best throughout the tournament.

title: Death penalty by lethal injection, shooting or electrocution? SC rejects plea
content: The Supreme Court declined to abolish hanging as an execution method.  New scientific evidence could prompt future reconsideration of this decision.  The court permitted the Centre to form an expert panel.  This panel will examine alternative execution methods for reduced pain.  Hanging remains the current method while reviews are pending.

title: Bangladesh does not want Teesta dispute to hurt ties with India, says minister
content: The Teesta begins in the Himalayas and flows through Sikkim and West Bengal before entering Bangladesh. It eventually joins the Jamuna, which is the Bangladeshi name for the Brahmaputra. The river is particularly important to northern Bangladesh, where farmers depend on its water. It is also important to West Bengal for irrigation and power generation, with several districts in North Bengal relying on its waters.

title: IAS officer who helped turn India's software industry into global powerhouse
content: N Vittal, the IAS officer and former Secretary of the Department of Electronics, played a key role in shaping India's software industry by removing regulatory barriers and promoting shared digital infrastructure. The article traces how a 1985 Texas Instruments satellite link, famously transported by bullock cart in Bengaluru, demonstrated India's potential for global software exports. Vittal later championed Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), helping companies access communication infrastructure, hardware and global markets while accelerating India's IT revolution.

title: BJP, SP rivals take their electoral battle to wrestling pit, score love-all
content: During the vibrant Nag Panchami celebrations, political adversaries Aman Yadav and Ram Singh Kallu took to the mat for an intense wrestling match that lasted fifteen minutes. Despite their fierce competition, neither wrestler emerged victorious, leading to an official draw. Their cash prize was equally split, marking a unique moment of camaraderie amid their political rivalry at the Bachau Veer Akhara on the Banaras Hindu University grounds.

title: India eyes first cargo ship along Arctic Route to Russia - why it matters
content: Located along Russia’s Arctic coastline, Arkhangelsk lies on the Northern Dvina River and serves as a major cargo centre connected to the Northern Sea Route. The NSR stretches about 5,600 km across Russia’s Arctic waters. Much of the route remains covered by thick ice for most of the year.

title: 'Awarapan 2' eyes Rs 100cr in India by Day 5 amid 'Batwara 1947', 'Spider-Man' buzz
content: Awarapan 2 experienced a decline in box office sales on Monday following a robust opening weekend. The film has garnered a net of Rs 92.81 crore in India thus far, while its global earnings stand at Rs 130.82 crore after four days. This sequel is outperforming Batwara 1947 but faces stiff competition from the Hollywood blockbuster Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

title: 18 years of ruthless Virat Kohli: The man who refused to stay ordinary
content: Virat Kohli's career began with a modest debut in 2008.  He achieved numerous accolades, including World Cups and the Asia Cup.  Kohli then captained India to significant Test match victories overseas.  He broke Sachin Tendulkar's ODI century record during the 2023 World Cup.  Kohli retired from Tests and T20Is after winning IPL titles.

title: Woman dies after husband gives electric shocks to private parts
content: A 32-year-old woman named Nasreen died after alleged electrocution by her husband.  Her husband Israr reportedly administered electric shocks during a dispute over ancestral land.  Nasreen's family property was being pressured for sale by her in-laws.  An FIR was filed against Israr and several other family members.  Israr has been arrested while other accused individuals remain absconding.

title: Delhi University PhD scholar booked for slapping professor
content: Delhi University has taken action against a PhD student, suspending him and prohibiting his entry after CCTV footage revealed him assaulting a professor. An official complaint has been lodged, and authorities are currently looking into the matter. The Democratic Teachers' Front has expressed outrage, urging for safety measures to protect educators in light of previous violent occurrences on campus.

title: 8 labourers killed as pick-up vehicle collides with truck in MP's Bhind
content: Eight laborers died and 32 others were injured in a vehicle collision. The accident occurred early Tuesday morning near Chhimka village on the Bhind-Gwalior National Highway. Their pick-up vehicle collided head-on with a dumper truck after swerving to avoid cattle. The laborers were returning home after completing paddy transplantation work in Gwalior. Rescuers quickly arrived and transported the injured to a local hospital for treatment.

title: India seeks WTO consultations over 50% US duties quota on quartz surface imports
content: In its August 14 communication to the WTO, New Delhi said it has a "substantial interest" in the matter and suggested that the consultations be conducted.

title: ‘No state should interfere’: DKS warns Tamil Nadu over Chamarajanagar killings
content: Karnataka deputy chief minister warned Tamil Nadu politicians against interference.  He asserted Karnataka would protect its territorial sanctity and administration.  Tamil Nadu leaders demanded a high-level probe into the August 15 firing incident.  Karnataka officials stated forest personnel returned fire in self-defense.  The state has ordered a magisterial inquiry and offered interim relief.

title: Delhi HC puts JNU admissions on hold over deprivation points
content: The Delhi High Court has put JNU’s 2026-27 admissions based on deprivation points on hold, questioning whether the university can effectively add marks to CUET scores after the entrance examination. Under JNU’s policy, eligible candidates can receive up to 12 deprivation points, equivalent to 36 marks. JNU defended the system as a measure to ensure representation from across India, while a petitioner challenged its legality. The court will hear the matter again on August 24, 2026.

title: 'Take Gyanesh Kumar to US': Cong's jibe after Trump praises India's poll system
content: Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera took aim at Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's views on US voter identification rules, highlighting a comment made by Donald Trump that praised India's election system. With a hint of sarcasm, Khera proposed sending India’s electronic voting machines and Kumar to the US. This debate highlights ongoing tensions between Congress and the Election Commission, particularly regarding accusations of vote theft during past Lok Sabha elections.

title: From Su-30MKI to T-90: India adds 405 defence items to ‘make at home’ list
content: The Department of Defence Production has added 405 items to its positive indigenisation list. This move aims to boost self-reliance in defence production and generate business for domestic manufacturers. The list includes various weapons, platforms, and electronic systems for future sourcing. Indian industry, especially MSMEs, will play a significant role in this indigenisation process. This initiative aligns with the broader Aatmanirbhar Bharat push in defence manufacturing.

title: TISS names new chief guest weeks after CJI visit sparked 'protest fears'
content: The Tata Institute of Social Sciences has rescheduled its 86th convocation for August 22.  Dr C S Pramesh will now be the chief guest at the postponed event.  The original ceremony was abruptly cancelled just two days before its scheduled date.  Students faced financial losses due to the sudden postponement of their graduation.  The institute has assured reimbursement for eligible travel and accommodation expenses incurred.

title: ‘No safe harbour if law violated’: Govt’s message to Meta on content moderation
content: India has warned Meta that safe-harbour protection is not guaranteed if laws are violated. Discussions focused on content moderation and child sexual abuse material handling. The government seeks greater local sensitivity in content moderation decisions. Deepfakes and synthetically generated content require clear labeling for users. WhatsApp usernames are also being examined across all messaging platforms.

title: 14 of 28 CMs face serious criminal cases, Supreme Court told
content: Fourteen chief ministers face serious criminal cases, with Telangana's leader having the most. Many legislators across states also have pending criminal charges against them. In Lok Sabha, 170 MPs and Rajya Sabha, 75 members face criminal cases. Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of pending criminal cases against legislators. Special courts are requested to expedite trials for these elected officials.

title: Clean chit to Champat Rai? SIT submits Ayodhya temple theft report
content: The Uttar Pradesh home department has submitted the SIT's final report on the Ayodhya temple donation theft. This report was handed over to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust for further action. A three-member SIT, formed at the Trust's request, conducted the investigation. The preliminary report led to an FIR naming eight individuals as accused. The SIT's findings also guided subsequent arrest actions in the case.

title: BJP names in-charges for poll-bound UP, Punjab & Gujarat
content: the BJP appointed state in-charges for poll-bound Uttar Pradesh and Punjab . the saffron party will seek a third consecutive term . BJP national president Nitin Nabin appointed national general secretary and national secretary Vinod Tawde .

title: 'This is the right way': Rahul welcomes end of Jharkhand students’ hunger strike
content: leader of opposition in Lok Sabha calls for changes to the existing system . he says he stood with every student in the country and called for changes . the students had exercised restraint and made their concerns heard, he said .

title: 'I apologise on his behalf': Vijay after minister's Karunanidhi reference
content: state forest minister apologises on minister's behalf for reference to late DMK leader . he refers to former CM and patriarch late M Karunanidhi by name . the reference triggered protests from opposition DMk members .

title: 'Got trapped in crowd': Bihar govt defends constable who fired AK-47 during protests
content: a constable deployed during student protests in Siwan fired four rounds from an AK-47 only after he was "trapped and surrounded by protesters" the government said the firing was directed into the air and did not injure any protesters . affidavit says the incident took place near JP Chowk in siwan .

title: ‘High-powered committee to probe alleged Delhi Police excesses on students’: SC
content: the bench will pass the order on Wednesday after receiving suggestions from the parties on other members to be included in the panel . the bench also said it will direct the authorities to hand over video footage and CCTV recordings of the violence during the July 20 Parliament march in Delhi .

title: A Costa Rican mother saved for 9 years to buy land, then built her home
content: econews Cindy Mora abarca spent 9 years saving money for a small plot of land in the Lámparas neighbourhood of Alajuelita, near San José, Costa Rica . she eventually secured the land through a loan, but that left her without enough money to construct a house on it . the project turned thousands of kilograms of discarded plastic into the walls of a real family home .

title: Delhi Police reject claims of 'excessive force' at Jantar Mantar student protest
content: the police deny using 'excessive force' during a march by students from Jantar Mantar to parliament on July 20 . the protesters turned violent and broke through several layers of barricades while attempting to proceed towards Parliament . police also rejected allegations that personnel used lathis fitted with nails .

title: 'Dignity of CM blown away': DMK targets Vijay over Trisha's I-Day front-row seat
content: DMK mouthpiece slams chief minister for 'fear that came to CM in three months' critics say the actress's pride was blown away when he hoisted the flag . the attack came through the mouthpiece Murasoli, whose editorial took aim at Vijay .

title: Property of paper-leak accused to be seized? SC seeks govt response over PIL
content: a bench of justices issued notice to the union of India and the states on a plea filed by advocate Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay . the plea also sought directions for a comprehensive assessment of the properties held by alleged perpetrators and their families .

title: Russia warns UK over Ukraine drone supplies, says Britain will face ‘consequences’
content: ANI Russia warns Britain it will pay a 'price' for its support for Ukraine . embassy in London accuses the country of 'deliberately opting for an escalation' the warning follows reports in the Times and Sunday Times that British-made drones had been used by Ukraine in long-range strikes .

title: Blast near Kabul school injures around 50 children; UN condemns 'heinous' act
content: a hand grenade explosion near school in dasht-e-Barchi injured at least 50 children . local media reports put the number of injured at around 50 children, though the figure has not been independently verified . the blast occurred around 4.30pm local time near the school, with several injured students taken to a nearby hospital .

title: 'Move Imran Khan to hospital': Pakistan SC directs govt amid ex-PM's health concerns
content: imran Khan, 73, has been in jail since august 2023 . he has been convicted in several cases that he and his supporters have described as politically motivated . his party welcomed the court order, saying it should have come earlier .
